body:
Do the LOCAL results of a Search wait for the CATALOGUE? No (decided with a test on main 3b820e1, 14 Nov 2026; branch task/search-local-results-never-wait). The 35 s blank page was not the catalogue.

TEST (app/test/features/search_local_first_test.dart, whole app through pumpApp, catalogue = the new FakeCatalogue.slow(), online network):
1. The catalogue's search is asked and never answers. The library holds artist Eminem and its song. One second after typing: Top result "Artist, Eminem" and the song row are on screen, no spinner, and the catalogue was asked exactly once (so this is the slow line, not the offline path). PASSES on the current code.
2. The catalogue answers late. Its song joins the list, and in each of 12 frames after the answer the library's Top result and song are still there, no spinner. PASSES.
Both can fail: (A) search_results.dart:74 changed to also wait for catalogue.isLoading: both fail. (B) library rows dropped once the catalogue has a value: test 2 fails. Reverted both; no product code changed.

WHY: SearchResultsView draws as soon as searchResultsProvider has a value; catalogueSearchProvider is only read for .value / .isLoading; the spinner shows only when nothing at all was found. searchResultsProvider (providers.dart:441) watches no catalogue provider.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE 35 s: "not even No results" can only be search_results.dart:74 (`!local.hasValue` -> empty box), so the LOCAL search itself had no value for 35 s. NOT proven why. Candidates: (1) the emulator's CPU load (my first guess, unproven); (2) searchResultsProvider watches artistTypoIndexProvider -> artistsProvider, a drift stream that emits again on every song write (own comment at providers.dart:413-415); each emission restarts the search, and a NEW query has no previous value to show, so while a sync or downloads write continuously, the first answer of a new query could be pushed back again and again (blank page until the writes pause); (3) drift's single connection queue behind a long write. Offline being instant fits (1) and (3) as well as (2): do not read it as a proof of any.

NEXT TEST (not done here, outside this task): a widget test that inserts a track every 100 ms while a search is open and expects the library rows within about 1 s. If it fails, fix at the provider: the first answer must come from the FTS alone, and the artists list may only feed the typo fallback afterwards. If it passes, measure on the emulator with the sync running (adb/logcat timestamps of the provider's start and end).
